claims.text: The proposed intervention is an in situ laser re-melting pass applied immediately after deposition of each layer.
The re-melting pass should use a tuned energy density to selectively reheat and re-melt the top layer.
Standard laser-additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components exhibit interlayer porosity.
Standard laser-additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components exhibit microstructural inhomogeneity and residual stresses.
Layer-by-layer laser re-melting reduces pore size and pore density.
Layer-by-layer laser re-melting enhances interlayer fusion.
Layer-by-layer laser re-melting refines grains through localized thermal re-mixing and stress relief.
The additional thermal energy re-mixes partially solidified material, fills voids, and homogenizes the microstructure.
Reduced defects and residual stresses improve dimensional fidelity by reducing warping and shrinkage.
Minimizing brittle defects and improving load transfer across layers increases mechanical integrity.
Relative to fabrication without re-melting, the intervention will lower porosity.
Relative to fabrication without re-melting, the intervention will reduce deviation from design dimensions by 10–20%.
Relative to fabrication without re-melting, the intervention will increase tensile strength by approximately 15–25%.
The beneficial effects should hold under an inert atmosphere at ambient pressure and moderate scan speeds and energy inputs typical of high-entropy-alloy processing.
Laser energy, scan speed, or atmosphere outside moderate ranges may cause melting instabilities or grain coarsening and negate the improvements.
Optimal laser re-melting parameters are specific to the high-entropy-alloy system.
